title: Master (engineer mode)
intro: The digital master of each side, e.g. the vinyl masters from the mastering studio as WAV or FLAC. After the analysis, every recording of the side is measured against it: speed, center hole, frequency response, level per track, clicks only on the vinyl, noise and pre-echo in the gaps.
approval_title: All copies against the master: checkpoints and recommendation, printable
common_loading: Loading the copy comparison for side {side} …
col_real_title: Clicks and pops in the music that the master does not explain
col_shared_title: Of these, also on another copy at the same spot
col_loud_title: Strength 80 and above: the ones you hear

common_hint.one: {n} spot sits at exactly the same place on several copies (±{tol} ms){all} (expected by chance: {random}). What is the same on all copies is in the stamper or the cut (or is tracing distortion at the same spot in the music); what is on one copy only belongs to that copy (dust, static, pressing defect).
common_hint.other: {n} spots sit at exactly the same place on several copies (±{tol} ms){all} (expected by chance: {random}). What is the same on all copies is in the stamper or the cut (or is tracing distortion at the same spot in the music); what is on one copy only belongs to that copy (dust, static, pressing defect).

common_spots: Shared spots (the {n} most important: on the most copies first, then the strongest)
play_master_title: The same spot in the master
no_master_for_side: No master is stored for side {side}: upload it on the record page under “Master (engineer mode)”.
duration_hint: A side takes one to two minutes.
echo_post_title: End of the music, then the echo
head_done: Master: {name} · {anchors} anchors, quality {quality} · computed in {secs} s
stat_grade_sub: same calculation as the grade, without false alarms (what the master identifies as music) · without master: {grade}
stat_clicks_sub: in the music, {pops} of them pops · {master} of {total} detections there are music · {quiet} in quiet passages (not graded)
stat_treble: Treble at the end of the side
stat_treble_sub: at 10 kHz relative to the start
loud_summary: The loudest real clicks ({n} at strength {threshold} or more, to listen to)
loud_hint: Clicks the master does not explain, by strength. These are the ones you hear. Click false alarms in the click chart and mark them as such.
freq_hint: Per third of the side, relative to 1 kHz, groove noise subtracted. This also contains the response of cartridge and preamp (see turntable check). What changes from start to end is the inner-groove loss. Dashed: the stereo component (L−R) in the middle of the side. If it falls off in the bass, the bass was made mono for cutting.
col_relative_title: Deviation from the average of the tracks
levels_hint: Difference vinyl to master per track, relative to the average (the overall loudness depends on the turntable, vinyl {gain} dB). Spread {spread} dB.
wow_hint: Time offset against the master every 50 ms, fitted with an oscillation of the revolution period ({rev} s). An off-center hole changes the groove speed by ±offset/radius, so it grows towards the inside. {verdict} Around 0.1 mm it can also be the play of the hole on the spindle: put the record on again and record once more; if the value stays, it is the pressing.
col_pre_echo_title: Copy of the following entry one revolution earlier
col_post_echo_title: Copy of the ending one revolution later
gaps_hint: Where the master is silent, everything on the vinyl is noise or echo. Noise from the quietest 40 % of the gap (echo and clicks do not count). Echo level relative to the music; an echo counts as found if it lies exactly one revolution away from the music. In brackets: the value when nothing was found.
clicks_summary: Clicks on the vinyl only (the {n} strongest, to listen to)
col_residual_title: What remains of the peak after subtracting the master
clicks_hint: For each detected click, the master is matched to the recording at that spot and subtracted. If a sharp peak remains, it is a defect on the vinyl; otherwise it belongs to the music. ▶ Vinyl and ▶ Master play the same spot.
